# Door reference

<!-- Generated by `node tools/door-reference.mjs --write` from crates/endpoint/src. Do not edit by hand: CI fails when this page differs from the generated one. -->

This page lists every tool the AI door answers: 13 core tools and 75 verbs in 18 packs. It is printed from the Rust source by `tools/door-reference.mjs`, so a renamed argument, a new refusal or a new verb changes the page; `node tools/door-reference.mjs --check` fails when the checked-in file is stale. Start with the [AI door page](ai-door.md) for how a session works.

## How the page is made

The generator is a small text parser, not a running server. It reads the `e2_tool!` macros and `impl ToolBase` blocks, the `VerbSpec::of` registrations, the argument structs and the refusal sites in the handler of each verb and in the same-file functions that handler calls. What it quotes is what the source says:

- **Scope** is the capability card the verb registers with, plus the read-only hint of its annotations.
  - `observe`: Read/compute tools: admitted, no capability spend, no journal write.
  - `propose`: `tx.preview`: shape validation plus EXPLAIN dry-run, writes nothing.
  - `commit`: `tx.apply`, `scene.place`: mask, scope, budget, then EXPLAIN.
  - `revert`: `tx.undo`: newest-batch journal revert as a new revision.
- **Ranges** are quoted from the description and from the refusal messages that name the argument. The handler's validation is the authority; a range the source never writes in text does not appear here.
- **Typed refusals** are the `code` plus the message template of each refusal site. A `{NAME}` that is a constant in the crate is filled in; other placeholders stay as written.
- **Undo** is `none` for a read-only verb and `this verb is the undo` for a `revert` verb. Otherwise it quotes the description sentence that says undo, or says `journaled` when the handler calls `apply_gated` (the path of `tx.apply`, which `tx.undo` reverts), or says `not stated in the source`.

## Refusals every call can get

From the pack dispatch (`packs/mod.rs`):

| Code | Message |
|---|---|
| `bad_args` | args for `{name}` do not fit its input schema ({error}); re-run after api.describe `{name}` for the schema |
| `bad_output` | `{name}` produced output outside its schema ({error}); re-run and report the verb |
| `unknown_verb` | verb `{verb}` is served by no pack ({}); re-run api.search for the verb, then api.describe `pack:<name>` for its exact names |
| `unknown_pack` | pack `{pack}` is unknown; the door serves packs [{}]; re-run with one of those names |
| `tool_budget_exceeded` | api.load refused: loading pack `{}` would advertise {reach} tool chars; the tool budget is 66500 chars with 2048 kept as headroom, so a list may cost at most {MAX_ADVERTISED_CHARS}; unload a pack first (api.load unload:true) or load a smaller one |

From the capability gate (`tool_capabilities.rs`, the refused cases of its adversarial briefs), seen on the `commit` and `propose` verbs:

| Code | First brief that triggers it |
|---|---|
| `empty_batch` | `preview_empty (no ops)` |
| `too_many_ops` | `preview_too_many (257 inserts)` |
| `op_not_allowed` | `commit_insert_mask_none` |
| `out_of_scope` | `commit_insert_out_of_scope` |
| `over_budget` | `commit_over_budget (2 ops, budget 1)` |
| `destructive_tier` | `commit_remove_tier_zero` |
| `unknown_tool` | `` door_unknown_shell (`shell.exec`) `` |
| `needs_write_gate` | `` write_gate_bare_preview (`tx.preview`) `` |

## Core tools

These are always advertised.

| Tool | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [`scene.read`](#sceneread) | `observe` · read-only · always advertised | Bounded scene snapshot: document revision plus stable-id rows (id, parent, local pose). |
| [`tx.preview`](#txpreview) | `propose` · read-only · always advertised | Dry-run a command batch: validate and diff with no side effects. |
| [`tx.apply`](#txapply) | `commit` · always advertised | Atomically apply a previewed batch through the capability gate. |
| [`tx.undo`](#txundo) | `revert` · always advertised | Undo the newest journaled batch as a new revision. |
| [`play.run`](#playrun) | `observe` · always advertised | Headless arena match job: action=start runs a bounded match, poll reads progress then the checkpoints, cancel stops a running job. |
| [`capture`](#capture) | `observe` · read-only · always advertised | Renderer receipt (manifest plus PNG bytes) when a capture callback is wired; structured unsupported otherwise. |
| [`api.search`](#apisearch) | `observe` · read-only · always advertised | Search the engine index (API, tools, assets, scenes) with BM25. |
| [`api.describe`](#apidescribe) | `observe` · read-only · always advertised | Describe one indexed path: signature, docs, units, owner, callers. |
| [`api.call`](#apicall) | `observe` · writes · always advertised | Call one pack verb by exact name with its typed args; the verb's own gates, audit record and undo apply. |
| [`api.load`](#apiload) | `observe` · writes · always advertised | Load one verb pack so tools/list advertises its verbs (unload hides them again); verbs stay callable by name either way. |
| [`test.run`](#testrun) | `observe` · read-only · always advertised | Run the structured harvest checks (scene, preview, budget, manifest, log) with no side effects. |
| [`sim.build_encounter`](#simbuild_encounter) | `observe` · read-only · always advertised | brief text to validated encounter plan: goals, move rows, difficulty rung |
| [`game.build`](#gamebuild) | `observe` · read-only · always advertised | brief text to packaged playable slice: level, character, encounter, five-minute play proof |

### `scene.read`

> Bounded scene snapshot: document revision plus stable-id rows (id, parent, local pose). Paged by cursor/limit; read-only, no side effects.

- **Scope:** `observe` · read-only · always advertised
- **Undo:** none: read-only
- **Source:** `crates/endpoint/src/mcp_tools.rs`
- **Returns:** `SceneReadOutput` with `revision`, `total`, `cursor`, `returned`, `truncated`, `objects`

**Arguments** (`SceneReadArgs`):

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range quoted from the source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | `Option<u32>` | no |  | `1..=128`; Page size, 1..=128 (default 64). |
| `cursor` | `Option<u32>` | no |  | Page start as an object offset (default 0). |

**Typed refusals:**

| Code | Message |
|---|---|
| `bad_limit` | limit {limit} is outside 1..=128 (default 64) |
| `bad_cursor` | cursor {cursor} is beyond {total} objects |
| `snapshot_failed` | node {id} vanished mid-read; retry scene.read |
| `snapshot_failed` | node {id} holds a non-finite pose; refusing to serialize it |

### `tx.preview`

> Dry-run a command batch: validate and diff with no side effects. Returns effects, the resulting revision and a single-use approval for tx.apply.

- **Scope:** `propose` · read-only · always advertised
- **Undo:** none: read-only
- **Source:** `crates/endpoint/src/mcp_tools.rs`
- **Returns:** `TxPreviewOutput` with `effects`, `resulting_revision`, `action_hash`, `approval`

**Arguments** (`TxPreviewArgs`):

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range quoted from the source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `expected_revision` | `u64` | yes |  | Must equal the document revision, else nothing runs. |
| `idempotency_key` | `u64` | yes |  | Retry identity, echoed back to `tx.apply`. |
| `ops` | `Vec<OpDto>` | yes |  | `1..=64`, `1..=256`, `at most 256`; Edits in order, 1..=256 entries. |

**Typed refusals:**

| Code | Message |
|---|---|
| `bad_id` | ops[{index}].{field} `{text}` is not an object id (expected UUID text; the nil id `{nil}` means 'no parent' on parent fields) |
| `bad_pose` | ops[{index}].local holds a non-finite lane; poses must be finite (meters position, quaternion, scale) |
| `bad_id` | ops[{index}].id must not be nil; insert needs a fresh id |
| `bad_material` | ops[{index}].material `{text}` is not a material name ({error}; expected 1..=64 bytes of 0-9 A-Z a-z - _ .; null clears the binding) |
| `bad_component` | ops[{index}].value for `{}` is refused: {error} |
| `bad_component` | ops[{index}].component `{name}` is not a component schema; the schemas are [{}]; re-run with one of those |
| `empty_batch` | ops holds 0 entries; submit 1..=256 ops |
| `too_many_ops` | ops holds {} entries; at most 256 per transaction |

### `tx.apply`

> Atomically apply a previewed batch through the capability gate. Requires the tx.preview approval; idempotency-keyed and revision-checked. Denied, stale or duplicate calls write nothing.

- **Scope:** `commit` · always advertised
- **Undo:** journaled: the handler calls `apply_gated`, so core `tx.undo` reverts the newest batch
- **Source:** `crates/endpoint/src/mcp_tools.rs`
- **Returns:** `TxApplyOutput` with `revision`, `effects`, `key`, `journal_index`, `undo_token`, `changes`, `spatial_delta`

**Arguments** (`TxApplyArgs`):

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range quoted from the source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `expected_revision` | `u64` | yes |  | Must equal the document revision, else nothing runs. |
| `idempotency_key` | `u64` | yes |  | Same key as the previewed batch. |
| `ops` | `Vec<OpDto>` | yes |  | `1..=64`, `1..=256`, `at most 256`; Same ops as the previewed batch. |
| `approval` | `ApprovalDto` | yes |  | Approval minted by `tx.preview` for this exact batch. |
| `delta` | `Option<bool>` | no |  | `false` skips the spatial delta (default true). |

### `tx.undo`

> Undo the newest journaled batch as a new revision. A given undo_token must match the newest batch key.

- **Scope:** `revert` · always advertised
- **Undo:** this verb is the undo
- **Source:** `crates/endpoint/src/mcp_tools.rs`
- **Returns:** `TxUndoOutput` with `revision`, `undone_key`, `effects`

**Arguments** (`TxUndoArgs`):

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range quoted from the source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `undo_token` | `Option<u64>` | no |  | When given, must match the newest batch key (decimal string or number in). |

| Code | Message |
|---|---|

| `undo_mismatch` | newest undoable batch is key {}, not token {token}; omit undo_token to undo the newest batch |

## Pack `scene`

layout authoring: brief, spatial findings, intent placement, brief-to-level build, spatial questions, the digest watch, the next-call planner, pointing at a capture and the BRP component filter

Listed in a fresh session: yes. Source: `crates/endpoint/src/packs/scene.rs`.

| Verb | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [`scene.brief`](#scenebrief) | `observe` · read-only | Bounded scene brief: digest plus stable text rows. |

### `scene.query`

> Spatial questions with reasons: near, between, visible, reachable, cover_near, largest_open, free_space, cone, relation, view, lidar, map, pixel. Read-only; api.describe query:&lt;kind&gt; gives a working call.

- **Scope:** `observe` · read-only
- **Undo:** none: read-only
- **Source:** `crates/endpoint/src/scene_query.rs`
- **Returns:** `SceneQueryOutput` with `kind`, `digest`, `bytes`, `truncated`, `count`, `repeat_count`, `hits`, `ids`, `conflicts`

**Arguments** (`SceneQueryArgs`):

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range quoted from the source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `String` | yes |  | Question. Needs: near anchor; between anchor, other; visible eye_m; reachable anchor; cover_near anchor, eye_m; largest_open -; free_space -; cone half_angle_deg, anchor\|eye_m; relation anchor, relation; sees anchor, other; why_hidden anchor, eye_m; clearance anchor; slide anchor, dir; ground eye_m; measure anchor, other; room_of anchor; in_room room; exits_of anchor\|room; glance eye_m; coverage anchor, eye_m; view eye_m; lidar eye_m; map eye_m; pixel eye_m. a\|b means either. |
| `anchor` | `Option<String>` | no |  | Object label from scene.brief (`lamp_2 [uuid]`) or bare UUID: the subject. |
| `other` | `Option<String>` | no |  | Second object label: far end for between, viewer for relation. |
| `radius_cm` | `Option<i32>` | no |  | Radius in cm, 1..=10000: search radius (default 500), slide range (500), clearance width needed (60), measure gap needed. |
| `eye_m` | `Option<[f32; 3]>` | no |  | Point [x, y, z] in meters: the eye for visible and cone, the threat for cover_near. |
| `yaw` | `Option<f32>` | no |  | Facing in radians, 0 = +X (visible, cone from eye_m); default 0. |
| `crouch` | `Option<bool>` | no |  | True to test crouched cover (cover_near). |
| `capsule_radius_cm` | `Option<i32>` | no |  | Clearance radius in cm, 0..=10000, default 30 (largest_open, free_space). |
| `min_gap_cm` | `Option<i32>` | no |  | Smallest gap between samples in cm, default 100 (free_space). |
| `max_samples` | `Option<u32>` | no |  | Spots to sample, default 8 (free_space). |
| `seed` | `Option<u64>` | no |  | Sampler seed, default 7 (free_space). |
| `limit` | `Option<u32>` | no |  | Most hits, 1..=64, default 64. |
| `budget_bytes` | `Option<u32>` | no |  | Answer budget in bytes, 1..=16384, default 4096. |
| `half_angle_deg` | `Option<i32>` | no |  | Cone half-width in whole degrees, 1..=180 (cone); half the field of view (glance, coverage). |
| `filter` | `Option<String>` | no |  | Keep cone rows whose label contains this text. |
| `relation` | `Option<String>` | no |  | Relation word: above, below, in_front_of, behind, left_of, right_of, against, around, aligned, near, far, visible_from, reachable_from. |
| `format` | `Option<String>` | no |  | Answer shape: rows (default, one row per hit), ids (labels of matched hits only), count (matched count only). |
| `matched_only` | `Option<bool>` | no |  | Drop unmatched rows. Default true for visible (pass false for blocked rows), false otherwise. |
| `dir` | `Option<String>` | no |  | Slide direction: +x, -x, +z, -z, up, down, +x+z, +x-z, -x+z, -x-z (slide). |
| `what` | `Option<String>` | no |  | gap (default), overlap, align or contain (measure). |
| `room` | `Option<u32>` | no |  | Room number from room_of (in_room, exits_of). |
| `pitch` | `Option<f32>` | no |  | Camera pitch in radians, up is positive (coverage). |
| `cells` | `Option<[i32; 4]>` | no |  | View or pixel box `[w, h, x, y]` in cells, edges 1..=128 (view, pixel; default [24,16,0,0], x and y inside the view). The map uses the eye as its center and `radius_cm` as its reach. |

### `play.step`

> Live duel step: take inputs for N ticks and return the state digest, per-fighter numbers (hp, stamina, phase, pos, yaw), the last combat events and a real capture PNG. Holds the match across calls (a longer prefix of the same tape only simulates the new ticks); same inputs twice give the same digests. upto_tick N simulates ticks 0..N and reports tick N with the checkpoint N-1 digest (the play.run tick_count/final_hash for the same prefix).

- **Scope:** `observe` · pack `rules` is listed after `api.load`
- **Undo:** not stated in the source
- **Source:** `crates/endpoint/src/play/play_session.rs`
- **Returns:** `PlayStepOutput` with `tick`, `digest`, `participants`, `inputs_applied`, `summary`, `manifest`, `png_bytes`, `fighters`, `events`, `timing`

**Arguments** (`PlayStepArgs`):

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Range quoted from the source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `seed` | `Option<u64>` | no |  | decimal string on the wire; Match seed (a decimal string or a number); same seed plus same tape replays the same digest. |
| `participants` | `Option<u8>` | no |  | `2..=32`; alias `fighters`; Participant count, 2..=`MAX_PARTICIPANTS`. |
| `half_extent_m` | `Option<f32>` | no |  | `5.0..=100.0`; Arena half-extent in meters, 5.0..=100.0, explicit (never defaulted across tools when comparing receipts). |
| `upto_tick` | `Option<u32>` | no |  | `0..N`, `1..=3600`; Ticks to simulate as the 1-indexed count N of the 0-indexed prefix `0..N` (1..=`MAX_PLAY_TICKS`); the digest is the checkpoint `N - 1` hash. See the module legend. |
| `inputs` | `Option<Vec<PlayInputDto>>` | no |  | `-100..=100`, `-18000..=18000`, `at most 2048`; Tape inputs with 0-indexed tick ids inside `0..upto_tick`. |
| `width` | `Option<u32>` | no |  | Receipt width in pixels, 1..=512 software. |
| `height` | `Option<u32>` | no |  | `1..=2048`, `up to 2048`; Receipt height in pixels, 1..=512 software. |
| `timing` | `Option<bool>` | no |  |  |

> Step the headless spar through a tape: seed, headcount, extent, tick count and inputs in; replay digest, per-fighter hp, stamina, phase, position, yaw and the newest hit/block/kill events out. A longer prefix of the same tape only simulates the new ticks. Same inputs replay the same digest; writes nothing.

## Pack `verify`

the verifiers at the door: resimulate a tape and bisect its first divergence, replay a proof bug bundle, summarize a traced proof tape, and run the verifier proof (A7 seeded bug plus mirror outcome digests)

Listed in a fresh session: no, call `api.load` with `verify`. Source: `crates/endpoint/src/packs/verify.rs`.

| Verb | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [`replay.verify`](#replayverify) | `observe` · read-only | Resimulate an arena tape against its recorded per-tick chain through the playtest replay body and report clean or the first divergent tick with both hashes. |
| [`replay.bisect`](#replaybisect) | `observe` · read-only | Binary-search a resimulated arena tape for the first tick whose hash leaves the recorded chain, through the playtest replay body. |
| [`bug.replay`](#bugreplay) | `observe` · read-only | Replay an engine-proof bug bundle (hex bytes) and report the authoritative first divergent tick with both checkpoint hashes. |
| [`trace.summary`](#tracesummary) | `observe` · read-only | Re-run an engine-proof tape (hex bytes) with tracing and return tick and event counts, the live-matching summary hash and a bounded digest. |
| [`verify.proof`](#verifyproof) | `observe` · read-only | Run the verifier proof through the door: bisect the A7 seeded bug tape to its seeded tick and digest every mirror task outcome, so a parity run compares this door with... |

## Coverage

88 tools parsed, 646 refusal rows printed, 0 declarations the parser could not read.
A verb whose handler converts a typed error defined in another file (the log tools, the level builder) shows fewer refusals than it can return; the tests next to its source are the full list.

Tools with no refusal site found: `capture`, `wound.table.get`, `material.list`, `asset.generate`, `sim.plan_goals`, `log.digest`, `log.query`, `rpc.discover`, `settings.get`, `session.activity`, `codex.search`.
